evidence: The user and their partner, Rui, spent two weeks in Japan from 11 to 25 April 2026: five nights in Tokyo, six in Kyoto and three in Osaka. It was their first trip to Asia.
They flew TAP from Lisbon to Tokyo via Frankfurt; the connection in Frankfurt was tight and their luggage arrived a day late.

pieces.body: Rui and I spent our first trip to Asia in Japan from 11 to 25 April 2026: five nights in Tokyo, six in Kyoto, and three in Osaka. We flew TAP from Lisbon to Tokyo via Frankfurt; the connection was tight and our luggage arrived a day late. In Kyoto, we stayed at the Hanaori ryokan near Gion, which was the highlight of the trip and somewhere I would like to return to; shojin ryori temple restaurants were the easiest vegetarian option for Rui. Finding vegetarian food in Osaka was harder than expected, but my favourite meal was at Tenkuu, a tempura counter in Osaka. I got a Suica card at the airport and topped it up twice; Rui twisted an ankle on the Fushimi Inari trail on 19 April and was fine after a few days. We spent about €6,200 total, slightly over our €5,500 budget, and I would book the JR Pass earlier next time because its price rose the week before I bought it. I want to return to Japan in autumn 2027 to see Hokkaido.
pieces.title: Japan trip with Rui, April 2026

header.title: Confidential recruiter pitch: Head of Platform role (via Brightline Talent)

evidence: On 1 October 2026 the user took a call from Dana Whitlock, a recruiter at Brightline Talent, about a Head of Platform role at a client she could not name yet.
The opportunity offered a base salary of €145,000–€165,000, a 15% annual bonus target and equity that Dana called "meaningful" without giving a number.
Dana said the hiring process would have four stages: a call with the CTO, a system design session, a leadership panel and a reference check.
pieces.body: On 1 October 2026, I discussed a confidential Head of Platform opportunity with Dana Whitlock at Brightline Talent for an unnamed Series C payments company in Lisbon with about 400 employees. The role would lead three platform teams of about 22 engineers across infrastructure, developer tooling, and internal APIs, report to the CTO, and be fully remote within Portugal with an optional Lisbon office; the client wants a January 2027 start. The proposed compensation was €145,000–€165,000 base, a 15% annual bonus target, and unspecified “meaningful” equity. The process would be a CTO call, system design session, leadership panel, and reference check. I am interested, but have not managed more than one team before and want the equity terms in writing before proceeding; I agreed to a follow-up call on 8 October 2026 after Dana confirms whether the client can disclose its name. I must keep the details confidential until the client agrees to reveal its name.
pieces.title: Confidential Head of Platform opportunity via Brightline Talent

evidence: The user is building Tern, a personal budgeting app for iPhone and Mac, as a side project with their friend Sofia Antunes, who handles the design. They started it in January 2026 and want a public TestFlight beta by the end of September 2026.
Tern imports bank exports as CSV and OFX files rather than connecting to banks directly, because the user does not want to store bank credentials or pay for an aggregator such as Plaid.
The app is written in Swift with SwiftUI and SwiftData; the user tried Core Data first but switched in March because the migration code was getting too complex.
pieces.body: I am building Tern, a personal budgeting app for iPhone and Mac, as a side project with my friend Sofia Antunes, who handles design. We started Tern in January 2026 and want a public TestFlight beta by the end of September 2026; I spend Sunday mornings on it, about four hours a week. Tern imports CSV and OFX bank exports instead of connecting directly to banks because I do not want to store bank credentials or pay for an aggregator such as Plaid. Tern uses Swift, SwiftUI, SwiftData, and CloudKit’s private database for device sync; I switched from Core Data to SwiftData in March 2026 because the migration code was becoming too complex. Sofia and I agreed that Tern will support both system appearance and a dark, high-contrast look. The open problem is automatic transaction categorisation: keyword rules were too brittle, so I am testing an on-device classifier. Tern will be free with a one-time €9.99 unlock for multiple accounts, with no subscription; its private GitHub repository is currently under Sofia’s account. I was pointed to the migration plan documentation when I asked how to rename a SwiftData model property without losing data.
pieces.title: Tern personal budgeting app side project

pieces.body: I signed a freelance contract with Oakhurst Media, a Dublin podcast network, on 26 March 2026 to rebuild the iOS client of its listener app. The contract runs from 6 April through 30 September 2026 at €720 per day, for four days per week, keeping Fridays free for my other clients. I invoice monthly with payment due 30 days from invoice; I accepted those terms instead of my requested 15 days in exchange for the higher rate. Siobhán Kelly, Head of Product, is my contact, and Marek Novak is the engineering lead. I must send PDF invoices with the purchase order number to the accounts address, and I set up a template; electronic signatures are valid. The contract's NDA prevents me from publicly naming Oakhurst's unreleased features, although I may list Oakhurst as a portfolio client; intellectual property transfers to Oakhurst upon payment, and either party may terminate with 14 days' notice. I want to turn the Oakhurst Media contract into a longer engagement if the first release goes well.

The feedback forms gave the talk 4.6 out of 5; several people said the live demo was the best part, and two said the CRDT section was too fast.
The user met Karin Lund from the Swift Server Workgroup, who invited them to write a guest post for the Swift.org blog.
pieces.body: On 24 September 2026, I gave my first conference talk in English, “Offline-first sync without tears,” at NordicSwift 2026 in Oslo; previously, I had spoken only at local meetups in Lisbon. The 30-minute-plus-Q&A talk covered conflict resolution with CRDTs in a SwiftData app using Tern, and about 250 people attended. I rehearsed five times with my partner because I was nervous, which helped a lot; the organisers covered my flight and two hotel nights, while I paid for an extra night to see Oslo. The slides are on Speaker Deck and the recording was expected on YouTube in October 2026; feedback averaged 4.6/5, praising the live demo but noting that the CRDT section was too fast. I also met Karin Lund of the Swift Server Workgroup, who invited me to write a guest post for the Swift.org blog, and I had to ask the organisers for a USB-C-to-HDMI adapter.
pieces.title: NordicSwift 2026 talk in Oslo

evidence: The user wants to submit the same talk, with a slower CRDT section, to two more conferences in 2027, and would rather not do live demos again because the venue Wi-Fi nearly failed.

The MRI on 2 April 2026 at the Clínica Lumiar showed a grade 2 tear of the medial meniscus, with no ligament damage.

pieces.body: I injured my right knee playing five-a-side football on 14 March 2026, twisting it on landing and feeling a pop followed by swelling. An MRI at Clínica Lumiar on 2 April 2026 showed a grade 2 medial-meniscus tear with no ligament damage. Dr. Paulo Mendes advised against surgery for now and prescribed physiotherapy; I must not play football or run on hard surfaces until cleared, while cycling and swimming are fine. I stopped taking ibuprofen after ten days because it upset my stomach, and use ice and paracetamol when the knee flares up. I started physiotherapy with Joana Reis at Fisio Campo de Ourique on 8 April 2026, twice weekly, focusing on quadriceps and hip strengthening, balance, and gradually adding load; single-leg balance exercises are difficult for me and I tend to skip them at home. By mid-June 2026, I could walk for an hour without pain and climb stairs normally, but kneeling still caused discomfort. At my 20 July 2026 review, Dr. Mendes said my knee was healing well, cleared gentle jogging on grass or a treadmill from August 2026, and said football should wait until at least October 2026; I should continue home exercises three times weekly for another three months. Médis covered the MRI after a four-working-day pre-authorisation. I want to return to football but am considering padel because it may be easier on my knees.
pieces.title: Right knee meniscus injury and physiotherapy in 2026

The fourth-floor flat has a lift, and I chose it over a cheaper one-bedroom in Penha de França because I will use the second bedroom as my office. I must hand back my Graça flat by 15 November 2026 after giving notice on 30 September. The lease permits one pet, so my cat Miso can live there. I can replace the gas hob at my own cost, MEO fibre installation is booked for 3 November 2026 from 9:00 to 13:00, and I need to update my address with Finanças and my bank after moving. The landlord paid the estate agent's fee, and I measured the living room at 4.2 by 5.1 metres to plan the sofa placement.
pieces.title: Arroios flat lease and move

pieces.body: I completed Verdant Grid's interview loop for the Staff Data Engineer role during the week of 5–11 October 2026. The four interviews were on Tuesday 6 October and Thursday 8 October; Mette praised my enthusiasm and questions about data quality during a smart-meter pipeline system-design interview, while I was weaker in the live SQL exercise and ran out of time on the final window-function question. Jonas said the role is fully remote with an annual Copenhagen team week and uses Python, dbt, and Snowflake. Verdant Grid offered a salary range of DKK 85,000–95,000 per month; I like its energy-transition product but consider the pay below my freelance income, and would negotiate for DKK 100,000 per month if offered the role. I expected to hear back by Friday 23 October 2026.

El código de vestimenta es formal de verano; no habrá regalos, aunque se puede aportar al fondo de luna de miel en Japón, y quiero regalarles una noche del viaje. Marina Ocampo organiza la boda; debo confirmar asistencia en línea antes del 1 de marzo de 2027 y quiero comprar los pasajes antes de terminar 2026 para conseguirlos más baratos.

header.title: Recruiter call about a CTO role

evidence: Yesterday the user had a call with Marta Sousa, an independent recruiter, about a CTO position at Lumen Health, a 35-person Porto startup that makes appointment software for dental clinics. Marta asked the user to keep the conversation private, because the current CTO hasn't announced that he is leaving. The founders want someone who can still write code for the first year and grow the team from 6 to 15 engineers. The role pays €110,000 a year plus 1.5% equity vesting over four years, with a one-year cliff. It's hybrid, two days a week in the Porto office, which would mean commuting by train from Lisbon or moving. The company raised a €6M seed round in March and has about 20 months of runway. The stack is Kotlin on the backend and React on the web. There is no iOS app yet, and the founders would like the new CTO to start one.

The user said the equity sounded low for a CTO and asked whether there was room to negotiate; Marta thought 2% might be possible. The user is interested in the iOS work and in being a CTO, but is worried about the commute and about the runway.
The user wants to talk it over with their partner before deciding whether to continue, and told Marta they would reply by the end of next week.
pieces.body: On 1 September 2026, I spoke with independent recruiter Marta Sousa about the CTO position at Lumen Health, a 35-person Porto startup making appointment software for dental clinics. The conversation is private because Lumen Health's current CTO has not announced his departure. The hybrid role would require two days a week in the Porto office and involves coding during the first year, growing engineering from 6 to 15 people, Kotlin and React work, and starting Lumen Health's first iOS app. The proposed compensation is €110,000 annually plus 1.5% equity vesting over four years with a one-year cliff; I consider the equity low, and Marta Sousa thinks 2% may be negotiable. I am interested in the CTO and iOS work but concerned about the Lisbon–Porto commute and Lumen Health's roughly 20 months of runway; I will discuss it with my partner and reply to Marta Sousa by the end of the following week.
pieces.title: Lumen Health CTO recruiter call

evidence: The user plans to look up the founders on LinkedIn before replying. Marta said the founders would like an answer before the end of September, because they want the new CTO to start in January 2027. The role comes with a €3,000 yearly training budget, which the user would spend on conferences. The office is near São Bento station, about ten minutes' walk from the platform, so the train commute from Lisbon would be about three hours each way door to door.

The founders want my answer before the end of September 2026 and want the new CTO to start in January 2027. The role includes a €3,000 annual training budget that I would spend on conferences. Its office is near São Bento station, about a ten-minute walk from the platform, making a train commute from Lisbon about three hours each way door to door.
